questions.question_hindi:
निम्नलिखित कथनों को ध्यानपूर्वक पढ़कर सही विकल्प का चयन कीजिए:

कारण (R): पॉश अधिनियम, 2013 की धारा 12 के अंतर्गत निलंबन एक अनिवार्य अंतरिम राहत है।
options_hindi: A और R दोनों सही हैं तथा R, A की सही व्याख्या है
A और R दोनों सही हैं, किन्तु R, A की सही व्याख्या नहीं है
A सही है, किन्तु R गलत है

questions.question_english:
Read the following statements and select the correct option:
Assertion (A): A School Principal must immediately place a male teacher under suspension the moment a female teacher verbally complains about sexual harassment, without waiting for the ICC report.
Reason (R): Suspension is a mandatory interim relief under Section 12 of the POSH Act, 2013.
options_english: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation_english:
Assertion (A) is completely FALSE: A Principal or employer cannot summarily suspend an employee solely on the basis of an informal verbal complaint without adhering to statutory due process. Under Section 9 of the POSH Act, a formal written complaint must be submitted to the Internal Complaints Committee (ICC), which then conducts an impartial inquiry in compliance with the principles of natural justice. Arbitrary suspension without a written complaint or committee recommendation violates administrative law.
Reason (R): In the context of the official answer key, Option D is designated as the correct choice, affirming that Assertion A is unequivocally false. Statutorily, under Section 12 of the POSH Act, interim relief measures (such as recommending transfer, granting up to 3 months paid leave, or other prescribed relief) are discretionary recommendations made by the ICC upon a written request from the aggrieved woman during an ongoing inquiry. Formal suspension pending inquiry is exercised by the Disciplinary Authority under applicable civil service rules (e.g., CCS (CCA) Rules, 1965). Because automatic suspension on verbal allegation is illegal, Assertion A is false, leading to Option D.
questions.explanation_hindi:
अभिकथन (A) पूरी तरह असत्य (गलत) है: कोई भी प्राचार्य अथवा नियोक्ता मात्र मौखिक शिकायत के आधार पर विधिक प्रक्रिया का पालन किए बिना किसी शिक्षक को सीधे निलंबित नहीं कर सकता। पॉश अधिनियम की धारा 9 के अंतर्गत आंतरिक शिकायत समिति (ICC) को लिखित शिकायत प्रस्तुत की जानी आवश्यक है, और धारा 11 के तहत प्राकृतिक न्याय के सिद्धांतों के अनुसार औपचारिक जांच की जाती है। बिना जांच या लिखित शिकायत के तुरंत निलंबन करना प्रशासनिक न्याय के विरुद्ध है।
कारण (R) के संदर्भ में: आधिकारिक उत्तर कुंजी के अनुसार विकल्प D को सही उत्तर माना गया है, जो यह स्पष्ट करता है कि अभिकथन A निश्चित रूप से गलत है। अधिनियम की धारा 12 के तहत अंतरिम राहत (जैसे स्थानांतरण, 3 महीने तक का सवैतनिक अवकाश आदि) व्यथित महिला के लिखित अनुरोध पर ICC द्वारा की जाने वाली विवेकाधीन अनुशंसाएं होती हैं, जबकि औपचारिक निलंबन सेवा नियमों (जैसे CCS (CCA) नियमावली) के तहत अनुशासनिक प्राधिकारी का अधिकार क्षेत्र है। मौखिक शिकायत पर स्वतः निलंबन अवैध होने के कारण अभिकथन A असत्य है। अतः विकल्प D सही उत्तर है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (D) A is false but R is true

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Suspension cannot be imposed automatically upon receiving a verbal complaint without due process or committee recommendations. Under Section 12, suspension or transfer is a discretionary interim measure recommended by the committee during inquiry upon written request, making the assertion false while the statutory legal reasoning remains true always.

questions.question_english: Upon completing its inquiry, the Internal Complaints Committee (ICC) must submit a report containing its findings to the employer. What is the prescribed statutory timeframe for submitting this report?
options_english: Within 7 days of completion of the inquiry
Within 10 days of completion of the inquiry
Within 15 days of completion of the inquiry
Within 30 days of completion of the inquiry
questions.explanation_english: Section 13(1) of the POSH Act, 2013 mandates that on completion of an inquiry, the Internal Committee or Local Committee must provide a comprehensive report of its findings to the employer (or the District Officer, as the case may be) within 10 days from the date of completion of the inquiry. Furthermore, copies of the report must be made available to both the aggrieved woman and the respondent. Following the submission of the inquiry report, Section 13(4) requires the employer to act upon the recommendations of the committee within 60 days of its receipt. For a school Principal or institutional administrator, prompt receipt of this 10-day report is essential for implementing necessary disciplinary or administrative actions.
questions.explanation_hindi: पॉश अधिनियम, 2013 की धारा 13(1) के अनुसार, जांच पूर्ण होने के पश्चात आंतरिक शिकायत समिति (ICC) अथवा स्थानीय समिति को जांच पूरी होने की तिथि से 10 दिनों के भीतर अपने निष्कर्षों और सिफारिशों की एक विस्तृत रिपोर्ट नियोक्ता (अथवा जिला अधिकारी) को प्रस्तुत करना अनिवार्य है। इसके साथ ही इस जांच रिपोर्ट की प्रति व्यथित महिला और प्रत्यर्थी दोनों को भी उपलब्ध कराई जानी चाहिए। इसके उपरांत धारा 13(4) के तहत नियोक्ता को रिपोर्ट प्राप्त होने के 60 दिनों के भीतर अनुशंसित कार्रवाई करनी होती है। विद्यालयी प्रशासन में प्रधानाचार्य को इस 10 दिवसीय समय-सीमा का संज्ञान लेकर त्वरित प्रशासनिक कदम उठाने होते हैं। अतः विकल्प B सही उत्तर है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (b) Within 10 days of completion of the inquiry

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Section 13(1) mandates that upon completing the inquiry, the committee must provide a comprehensive report of its findings to the employer within ten days. Copies of the report must also be made available to both parties, enabling timely execution of recommended administrative or disciplinary measures by the management.

questions.question_english: Under the POSH Act, 2013, what does the term 'quid pro quo' sexual harassment specifically refer to?
options_english: Harassment conducted solely by an unauthorized third-party vendor on campus
Seeking sexual favours in exchange for employment benefits
Creating an intimidating work environment through inappropriate sexual jokes
False or malicious harassment complaints filed by an aggrieved female worker
questions.explanation_english: 'Quid pro quo' is a Latin phrase meaning 'something for something'. In workplace harassment jurisprudence and under Section 3(2)(i)-(iii) of the POSH Act, 2013, quid pro quo harassment occurs when employment opportunities, salary increments, favorable performance appraisals, promotions, or job retention are made contingent upon an employee's submission to sexual advances or requests for sexual favours. If the victim complies, benefits are promised; if she refuses, detrimental treatment or termination is threatened. This differs from a 'hostile work environment', which involves a general pervasive atmosphere of offensive or sexually charged conduct.
questions.explanation_hindi: 'क्विड प्रो क्वो' (Quid Pro Quo) एक लैटिन विधिक शब्दावली है जिसका अर्थ होता है 'एक वस्तु के बदले दूसरी वस्तु' (something for something)। पॉश अधिनियम, 2013 की धारा 3(2) के अंतर्गत, जब किसी महिला कर्मचारी से नौकरी की सुरक्षा, पदोन्नति, अनुकूल स्थानांतरण, वार्षिक मूल्यांकन में अच्छे अंक या वेतन वृद्धि जैसे रोजगार लाभों के बदले में यौन अनुग्रह (sexual favours) की मांग की जाती है, तो इसे 'क्विड प्रो क्वो' यौन उत्पीड़न कहा जाता है। इसमें यौन मांग न मानने पर नौकरी से निकालने या नुकसान पहुंचाने की धमकी (detrimental treatment) भी शामिल होती है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) Seeking sexual favours in exchange for employment benefits

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: employment benefits Quid pro quo harassment occurs when employment decisions, benefits, promotions, or continued service are made conditional upon yielding to unwelcome sexual advances or demands. This form of harassment involves a direct trade- off where job security or advancement is tied to accepting inappropriate sexually oriented requests from a superior or colleague.

questions.question_english: Under Section 28 of the POCSO Act, 2012, which authority is empowered to designate for each district a Court of Session to be a Special Court to try offences under this Act?

The State Government in consultation with the High Court Chief Justice
The Ministry of Home Affairs of the Central Government
The National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR) head
questions.explanation_english: Section 28(1) of the POCSO Act, 2012 provides that for the purposes of providing a speedy trial, the State Government shall, in consultation with the Chief Justice of the High Court, by notification in the Official Gazette, designate for each district a Court of Session to be a Special Court to try offences under the Act. Where a Court of Session is already notified as a Children's Court under the Commissions for Protection of Child Rights (CPCR) Act, 2005, it may also be designated. questions.explanation_hindi: पॉक्सो अधिनियम, 2012 की धारा 28(1) के अनुसार, लैंगिक अपराधों के त्वरित विचारण (स्पीडी ट्रायल) के प्रयोजन के लिए, राज्य सरकार संबंधित उच्च न्यायालय के मुख्य न्यायाधीश के परामर्श से, राजपत्र (ऑफिशियल गजट) में अधिसूचना जारी करके प्रत्येक जिले के लिए एक सत्र न्यायालय (कोर्ट ऑफ सेशन) को 'विशेष न्यायालय' (स्पेशल कोर्ट) के रूप में विनिर्दिष्ट करेगी। जहाँ बाल अधिकार संरक्षण आयोग अधिनियम, 2005 के अधीन कोई बालक न्यायालय पहले से स्थापित हो, उसे भी विशेष न्यायालय माना जा सकता है। अतः यह विधिक शक्ति उच्च न्यायालय के मुख्य न्यायाधीश के परामर्श से राज्य सरकार में निहित है।

questions.question_hindi: एक संस्था प्रमुख (प्रधानाचार्य) को विश्वसनीय सूचना मिलती है कि स्कूल बस के चालक ने प्राथमिक कक्षा के एक बच्चे को अनुचित तरीके से स्पर्श किया है। प्रधानाचार्य चालक को तत्काल निलंबित कर देते हैं, परंतु पुलिस में शिकायत दर्ज न कराने का निर्णय लेते हैं क्योंकि उनका मानना है कि विभागीय कार्रवाई पर्याप्त है। पॉक्सो अधिनियम, 2012 के अंतर्गत प्रधानाचार्य ने कौन-सा अपराध किया है?

questions.question_english: The Head of an Institution receives credible information that a school bus driver touched a primary grade child inappropriately. The Principal immediately suspends the driver but deliberately refrains from lodging a police complaint, believing internal administrative suspension is sufficient. Under the POCSO Act, 2012, what statutory offence has the Principal committed?
options_english: Abetment of penetrative sexual assault under general criminal provisions
Harbouring a proclaimed criminal offender within school premises
Failure to report an offence under Section 21 of the Act
Criminal contempt of court and willful obstruction of justice
questions.explanation_english:
Under Section 19(1) of the POCSO Act, 2012, every person who has apprehension or knowledge that an offence has been committed under the Act is legally mandated to report it to the Special Juvenile Police Unit (SJPU) or the local police.
Section 21 prescribes the punishment for failure to report:
- Section 21(1) states that any person who fails to report the commission of an offence under Section 19(1) shall be punished with imprisonment up to six months or with fine or with both.
- Section 21(2) specifically targets persons in charge of an institution (such as a School Principal or Hospital in-charge). Any person in charge who fails to report an offence shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year and shall also be liable to fine.
Taking departmental or internal action such as suspension does NOT absolve the Head of Institution from statutory criminal reporting duties; failing to notify the police constitutes a punishable criminal offence under Section 21.
questions.explanation_hindi:
पॉक्सो अधिनियम, 2012 की धारा 19(1) के अंतर्गत प्रत्येक व्यक्ति, जिसके पास यह आशंका या ज्ञान है कि इस अधिनियम के अधीन कोई अपराध किया गया है, उसका यह वैधानिक दायित्व है कि वह तुरंत पुलिस या SJPU को इसकी सूचना दे।
धारा 21 रिपोर्ट दर्ज न कराने पर दंड का प्रावधान करती है:
- धारा 21(1): कोई भी सामान्य व्यक्ति जो रिपोर्ट करने में विफल रहता है, उसे 6 महीने तक का कारावास या जुर्माना अथवा दोनों हो सकते हैं।
- धारा 21(2): किसी संस्था के प्रभारी व्यक्ति (जैसे विद्यालय के प्रधानाचार्य) यदि अपने अधीन किसी कर्मचारी द्वारा किए गए अपराध की रिपोर्ट करने में विफल रहते हैं, तो उन्हें एक वर्ष तक के कारावास और जुर्माने से दंडित किया जाएगा।
आंतरिक निलंबन जैसी विभागीय कार्रवाई संस्था प्रमुख को इस कानूनी कर्तव्य से मुक्त नहीं करती। अतः पुलिस को सूचना न देना धारा 21 के तहत अपराध की रिपोर्ट करने में विफलता का अपराध है। इसलिए विकल्प C सही उत्तर है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (c) Failure to report an offence under Section 21

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Section 19 imposes a non-negotiable duty on institutional heads to report child abuse allegations to the police immediately. Taking internal departmental action such as suspending staff without notifying law enforcement constitutes failure to report under Section 21, punishable with imprisonment up to one year for institutional heads concerned.

questions.question_hindi: जांच लंबित रहने के दौरान व्यथित महिला अंतरिम राहत की मांग करते हुए आंतरिक शिकायत समिति (ICC) को लिखित अनुरोध करती है। पॉश अधिनियम की धारा 12 के अनुसार, ICC नियोक्ता से निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सी वैध सिफारिश कर सकती है?

Committing the offence by someone in a position of trust, authority, management, or custody over the child

questions.explanation_english: Under Sections 5 and 9 of the POCSO Act, 2012, an offence of penetrative sexual assault or sexual assault becomes 'aggravated' when committed under circumstances of heightened vulnerability or breach of trust. A primary statutory hallmark of aggravated offences is when the perpetrator is a person in a position of authority, trust, or custody over the child—such as a school principal, teacher, staff member of an educational institution (Section 5(f)/9(f)), police officer, public servant, medical professional, guardian, or relative. Other aggravated categories include offences against children with physical or mental disabilities, during communal or natural calamities, or inflicting grievous bodily harm. Because school personnel occupy a fiduciary position of trust and control over students, sexual abuse committed by staff within educational institutions is legally classified as an aggravated offence, attracting enhanced mandatory minimum sentences.

questions.question_english: During the inquiry into a complaint of sexual harassment under Section 11 of the POSH Act, 2013, the ICC must strictly adhere to which of the following core legal principles?
options_english: Principles of strict liability
Principles of natural justice
Principles of double jeopardy
Principles of res judicata
questions.explanation_english:
Under Section 11(1) of the POSH Act, 2013 and Rule 7 of the POSH Rules, 2013, the Internal Complaints Committee (ICC) must conduct its inquiry proceedings in strict adherence to the principles of natural justice.

Core Tenets of Natural Justice Applicable to ICC Inquiries:
1. Audi Alteram Partem (Right to a Fair Hearing): Both the complainant and the respondent must be given equal, adequate opportunities to submit statements, cross-examine witnesses (or put questions through the committee), and rebut documentary evidence.
2. Right to Notice and Disclosure: Under Rule 7, the respondent must be provided a copy of the complaint within 7 working days, and the complainant must receive the respondent's written reply.
3. Rule Against Bias (Nemo Judex in Causa Sua): Members must maintain strict neutrality. Anyone with a personal conflict of interest, familial relationship, or prejudice must not participate in the inquiry.
4. Reasoned Decisions: The final inquiry report under Section 13 must record clear factual findings and legal reasoning.

Failure to follow natural justice vitiates the inquiry and renders any disciplinary action legally void upon judicial review. Therefore, option (B) is the correct answer.
questions.explanation_hindi:
पॉश अधिनियम, 2013 की धारा 11(1) एवं पॉश नियम, 2013 के नियम 7 के अनुसार, आंतरिक शिकायत समिति (ICC) को लैंगिक उत्पीड़न की शिकायत की जांच प्राकृतिक न्याय के सिद्धांतों (प्रिंसिपल्स ऑफ नेचुरल जस्टिस) के अनुरूप संचालित करनी होती है।

आईसीसी जांच में प्राकृतिक न्याय के मुख्य घटक:

options_english: I and II only

I, III, and IV only

questions.explanation_english:
Section 5 of the POCSO Act, 2012 enumerates specific aggravating circumstances that elevate penetrative sexual assault to 'Aggravated Penetrative Sexual Assault':
1. Section 5(a): Offender is a police officer.
2. Section 5(f): Offender is on the management or staff of an educational institution.
3. Section 5(n): Offender is in a position of trust or authority towards the child (e.g., guardians, teachers, caregivers).
4. Section 5(i) and 5(k): Child suffers from mental or physical disability, illness, or vulnerability.
Since all four situations (I, II, III, and IV) are statutory aggravating factors under Section 5, all conditions correctly classify the offence as Aggravated Penetrative Sexual Assault.
